objectives.text: Close the genocide question with Germany on Namibian terms. The 2021 joint declaration (recognition of the 1904-1908 killings and about EUR 1.1bn over 30 years, framed as development aid) was rejected in Namibia and never signed. President Nandi-Ndaitwah says the revised text is nearly finished, will go to parliament, and should be concluded by the end of 2026.

The EU green partnership was renewed for 2026-2030 in May 2026.

constraints.text: The German deal must pass a domestic test. The Landless People's Movement and eleven traditional authorities have asked the government attorney to set the joint declaration aside, and the Ovaherero Genocide Foundation opposes it; affected communities contest the government's monopoly on the negotiation. The National Assembly has been asked to be patient until the revised text is tabled.

paradoxes.text: The oil that pays for the state is also the fossil dependency that the EU green partnership is meant to replace. Namibia courts European green finance and Chinese and Western upstream capital at the same time, so the decarbonisation partner also profits from the new oil.

grand_strategy.reading: Namibia's strategy under Nandi-Ndaitwah is to convert its minerals and its new offshore oil into a revenue base while keeping every large patron in play: China for uranium capital, the EU for green hydrogen finance, the United States for trade access, and Germany for the historical settlement it cannot close without its own communities. The constraint that binds most tightly is domestic, since the genocide settlement and the land question require consensus that the government does not yet have. The land question is not researched in this pass and stays open.

stances.note: Germany is Namibia's development partner, and the 2021 joint declaration on the 1904-1908 genocide is the open wound: rejected in Namibia in 2021 and never signed. In April 2026 the president said the revised text had been reviewed by the chiefs' forum and a technical task force, was nearing conclusion and would be tabled in parliament, with the target of the end of 2026. Warming is our reading of that movement; partner is our reading of the structure (transactional, no alignment), not a source's word. Bond grievance is the historical wound, which stays open while communities contest the deal. Gap: the German side's 2026 position is not sourced in this pass.

stances_toward.note: Partner, stable. Ramaphosa met Nandi-Ndaitwah in Johannesburg in June 2026 (the Presidency describes the ties as cemented by strong economic interdependence, both countries being in SADC and SACU) and the two presidents co-chaired the 4th Bi-National Commission in Pretoria on 17 July 2026. Namibia is in SACU (since 1990) and the rand area, where the rand circulates alongside the Namibian dollar; Walvis Bay passed to Namibia on 1 March 1994; South African exports to Namibia were about USD 4.40bn in 2025 (Trading Economics, tier 4). The edge is Namibian resentment of a customs union in which Pretoria sets trade policy (an opinion piece of 2025, not used for the grade). The Namibia card holds no stance toward South Africa yet. Bond none: the liberation-movement tie is not read in the sources. Confidence C: the Presidency and DIRCO pages were seen only as search summaries.
